name: John Cale
description:
'''John Davies Cale''' (born 9 March 1942) is a Welsh singer, musician, composer, record producer and arranger. He was a founding member of the influential American [[Rock music|rock]] band [[the Velvet Underground]], with whom he recorded two studio albums. Over his six-decade career, Cale has worked in various styles of rock and [[avant-garde music]].

John Cale studied music at [[Goldsmiths, University of London]], before moving to New York City in 1963, where he performed as part of the [[Drone music|drone]] collective the [[Theatre of Eternal Music]] and formed the Velvet Underground with [[Lou Reed]]. Since leaving the band in 1968, Cale has released seventeen solo studio albums, including ''[[Paris 1919 (album)|Paris 1919]]'' (1973), which is retrospectively considered to be his masterpiece; ''[[Fear (John Cale album)|Fear]]'' (1974); ''[[Slow Dazzle (album)|Slow Dazzle]]'' (1975); and ''[[Music for a New Society]]'' (1982). In 1990, he collaborated with Reed on ''[[Songs for Drella]]'', a tribute to the Velvet Underground's mentor and one-time manager [[Andy Warhol]]. 

Cale has worked as a record producer with artists including [[Nico]], [[the Stooges]], [[the Modern Lovers]], [[Patti Smith]], [[Squeeze (band)|Squeeze]], [[Happy Mondays]] and [[Siouxsie and the Banshees]]. Cale was inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] as a member of the Velvet Underground in 1996.
